name: Heartbeat
summary: The agent is woken on a fixed interval (for example every 30 minutes), checks a short list of things to watch, and either does nothing or acts and reports. Hermes Agent ships it as a per-session /heartbeat prompt that fires only when the session is idle; OpenClaw used a HEARTBEAT.md checklist and in 2026 migrated it into ordinary automation jobs (a 'Proactive check' job).
how: A scheduler wakes the agent every N minutes
Agent reads its standing prompt or checklist (e.g. a /heartbeat prompt in Hermes; HEARTBEAT.md in older OpenClaw) and current context
Agent decides whether anything needs attention
If yes, it acts or messages the user; if not, it stays silent
Quiet hours and busy sessions suppress wakes
facts: Hermes Agent (/heartbeat, per session); OpenClaw (legacy; now a 'Proactive check' automation job, every 30 min by default)
Simple and general, but every wake costs a model call even when nothing changed
goodFor: Personal assistants that should notice things
watchOut: Token cost scales with wake frequency
Latency is bounded by the interval
Can become noisy without a silent-by-default rule
